title: Integral Kunneth short exact sequence for bounded derived abelian groups
statement:
Let $\mathrm{Ab}$ be the category of abelian groups and $D(\mathbf Z)=D(\mathrm{Ab})$ its cochain derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C,D\in D^b(\mathbf Z)$, meaning that each has nonzero cohomology in only finitely many degrees [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Use the ordinary K-flat derived tensor over $\mathbf Z$, obtained from [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $R=A=\mathbf Z$, and let $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z}_1$ be the first Tor group of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For every integer $r$ there is a short exact sequence of abelian groups, natural in both $C$ and $D$,
$$
0\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{i+j=r}H^i(C)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}H^j(D)
\longrightarrow H^r(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}D)
\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{i+j=r+1}\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z}_1(H^i(C),H^j(D))
\longrightarrow0.
$$
No finite-generation hypothesis on any cohomology group is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0H80, example-kunneth-dedekind, specializing R to Z; Tag 0H7Z, lemma-kunneth-spectral-sequence, whose hypothesis is C,D in D^b(R). Read in the local Stacks cache /home/ubuntu/c1-stacks-review/more-algebra.tex, lines 15800-15850.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-bounded-tensor-tor-spectral-sequence] with $R=\mathbf Z$ to the given bounded objects $C,D$. Its tensor construction is exactly the ordinary K-flat tensor specified in the item. Write $T^n=H^n(C\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}D)$. We obtain the pages
$$E_2^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{i+j=q}\operatorname{Tor}_{-p}^{\mathbf Z}(H^i(C),H^j(D)),$$
the differentials of bidegree $(s,1-s)$, and a finite decreasing filtration $F^pT^n$ with $F^pT^n/F^{p+1}T^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. The filtration and its graded identifications are natural in $C,D$. Boundedness of cohomology is precisely the input hypothesis of that node; no finite generation is required.

source.place: Tag 0H7Z, lemma-kunneth-spectral-sequence, statement and proof; Tag 0H7Y, proposition-kunneth-filtered

proof.text: We verify higher integral Tor vanishing rather than assuming a global-dimension assertion. For an abelian group $M$, take degree zero $P$ of Mathlib's projective resolution, with its epimorphic augmentation $\epsilon:P\to M$, and put $K=\ker\epsilon$. Projectivity makes $P$ flat, hence torsion free over $\mathbf Z$; its submodule $K$ is torsion free too. The PID (indeed Bezout-domain) torsion-free criterion [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] makes $K$ flat, without any finite-generation assumption. Construct explicitly the complex $F_1=K\hookrightarrow F_0=P$, $F_j=0$ for $j\ge2$, with the kernel inclusion as differential and $\epsilon$ as augmentation. Its degree-one kernel is zero, its degree-zero cokernel is $M$, and it has no higher homology. All its terms are flat. Apply [lem-pc-flat-resolution-tor-comparison] to this augmented flat resolution and any $N$. For $j\ge2$, the degree-$j$ term of $F\otimes N$ is zero, so its homology and therefore $\operatorname{Tor}_j(M,N)$ vanish. This presentation is used only for vanishing; no functorial choice of projective presentation or splitting is required for the exact-sequence arrows.

source.place: Tag 0H80, example-kunneth-dedekind, first assertion expanded using Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat, part (1), and the flat-resolution Tor comparison (Algebra Tags 00LY/00M1/00M3)

proof.text:
Step 2 kills the $E_2$ terms with $p\le-2$, and negative homological Tor degrees are zero by the convention of Step 1. Thus only columns $p=-1,0$ can survive. For $s\ge2$, an outgoing differential from either column has target column $p+s\ge1$, and an incoming differential has source column $p-s\le-2$. Both are zero. The successor-page homology rule [def-sp-spectral-sequence] now gives canonical identifications $E_{s+1}^{p,q}\cong E_s^{p,q}$ in every bidegree, by induction on $s\ge2$. Hence $E_\infty=E_2$. The degree-zero Tor identification in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] yields
$$E_\infty^{0,n}=\bigoplus_{i+j=n}H^i(C)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}H^j(D),\quad E_\infty^{-1,n+1}=\bigoplus_{i+j=n+1}\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z}_1(H^i(C),H^j(D)).$$
Every identification is canonical and commutes with the page maps, since homology of a zero differential is canonically the term itself. In Lean the Tor-zero identification is the canonical fromLeftDerivedZero isomorphism for the right-exact tensor functor. Its naturality in a natural transformation of tensor functors follows by computing on a projective resolution and cancelling the epimorphic opcycles projection. For the stationary pages, compose the zero-differential term-to-homology isomorphism with each successor-page isomorphism. Successor coherence of the given eventual graded identifications shows that transporting any sufficiently late page back to page two gives one fixed graded identification.

source.place: Tag 0H80, example-kunneth-dedekind, two-column degeneration; Tag 0H7Z, differential bidegrees

proof.text:
Fix $n$. Step 1 supplies a finite decreasing filtration, in the sense of [def-sp-filtration]. Since its graded pieces vanish outside $p=-1,0$, one has $F^pT^n=F^{p+1}T^n$ for $p\ge1$ and for $p\le-2$. Starting at an upper index where the finite filtration is zero and descending gives $F^1T^n=0$; starting at a lower index where it is all of $T^n$ and ascending gives $F^{-1}T^n=T^n$. Consequently the inclusion and quotient maps form
$$0\longrightarrow F^0T^n\longrightarrow T^n\longrightarrow T^n/F^0T^n\longrightarrow0.$$
Under the graded identifications of Step 1 and the calculation of Step 3, $F^0T^n=F^0T^n/F^1T^n$ identifies with the tensor direct sum, and $T^n/F^0T^n=F^{-1}T^n/F^0T^n$ identifies with the Tor-one direct sum. Define the left arrow as the inverse of the first graded identification followed by inclusion, and the right arrow as quotient followed by the second graded identification. This is exactly the asserted short exact sequence for $r=n$.

source.place: Tag 0H80, example-kunneth-dedekind, displayed short exact sequence; finite-filtration extraction from Tag 0H7Z

proof.text: For $u:C\to C'$ and $v:D\to D'$, the functoriality in [lem-kun-bounded-tensor-tor-spectral-sequence] gives $h=H^n(u\otimes^{\mathbf L}v):T^n\to (T')^n$ with $h(F^0T^n)\subseteq F^0(T')^n$. The inclusion square commutes because $h$ restricted to $F^0$ is the restriction of $h$ itself. The quotient square commutes because both routes send $x\in T^n$ to the class of $h(x)$ modulo $F^0(T')^n$. The graded identifications commute with these maps by the cited node, and Step 3's stationary-page identifications commute with them as well. Their maps on the two outside groups are therefore respectively $\bigoplus(H^i(u)\otimes H^j(v))$ and $\bigoplus\operatorname{Tor}_1(H^i(u),H^j(v))$. This proves naturality of both arrows in both derived arguments, with no choice of a splitting of the short exact sequence. For each graded degree and each pair of objects, use the maximum of their two stabilization bounds to compare both graded identifications with the same late page. Naturality of all stationary-page isomorphisms and the eventual graded comparison then gives naturality on page two. The direct-sum Tor-zero comparisons commute with the tensor maps, and the column minus one already has exactly the required Tor-one maps. Cancelling the canonical cokernel projections proves the inclusion and quotient naturality equations.

lean.statement: theorem integral_bounded_kunneth_exact (r : ℤ) : ∃ ι : ∀ C D : Bounded IntegralModuleCat.{u}, integralKunnethTensorTerm r C D ⟶ (homologyFunctor IntegralModuleCat.{u} r).obj (C.obj ⊗ D.obj), ∃ π : ∀ C D : Bounded IntegralModuleCat.{u}, (homologyFunctor IntegralModuleCat.{u} r).obj (C.obj ⊗ D.obj) ⟶ integralKunnethTorTerm r C D, (∀ C D : Bounded IntegralModuleCat.{u}, Function.Injective (ι C D) ∧ Function.Exact (ι C D) (π C D) ∧ Function.Surjective (π C D)) ∧ (∀ (C C' D D' : Bounded IntegralModuleCat.{u}) (f : C ⟶ C') (g : D ⟶ D'), integralKunnethTensorMap r f g ≫ ι C' D' = ι C D ≫ (homologyFunctor IntegralModuleCat.{u} r).map (f.hom ⊗ₘ g.hom)) ∧ (∀ (C C' D D' : Bounded IntegralModuleCat.{u}) (f : C ⟶ C') (g : D ⟶ D'), (homologyFunctor IntegralModuleCat.{u} r).map (f.hom ⊗ₘ g.hom) ≫ π C' D' = π C D ≫ integralKunnethTorMap r f g)
lean.note: Abelian groups in arbitrary universe u are encoded by ModuleCat.{u} (ULift.{u} ℤ), with the unique integral action. The tensor is the existing upstream K-flat derived monoidal tensor. The auxiliary definitions are the two direct sums and their canonical maps; the theorem gives a jointly natural family of short exact sequences, without finite generation or a chosen splitting.
